title: Francis' Testament
hook: the Lord gave me brothers, and no one showed me what to do
tomorrow: why would a mirror show you someone else's face?

segments.voice: The Canticle, read whole: sun, water, fire, earth, then people who forgive, and even Sister Bodily Death. Praised be, my Lord. Now Francis looks back on his own life, in his own words.

The group assignments go up, and your name sits next to three people you would never have chosen. Francis knew that moment from the other side. Looking back on his life, in a short text called his Testament, he remembers when everything changed. The Lord gave me brothers, he writes, and no one showed me what I ought to do. A few men turned up wanting to live the way he lived, and suddenly they were his. No plan. No manual. No one to ask. So what did he do with them?
screen: `NAMES YOU DIDN'T CHOOSE.` → `THE LORD GAVE ME BROTHERS.` → `NO ONE SHOWED ME WHAT TO DO.`

segments.voice: To answer, the Testament goes back further. When I was in sins, Francis says, it seemed very bitter to me to see lepers. And the Lord himself led me among them, and I showed mercy to them. And when I left them, what had seemed bitter was turned into sweetness of soul and body. That's where he places the start of his new life: not in a vision, but among people he'd been avoiding. Then the brothers arrive. Nobody showed him what to do, he says, but the Most High himself revealed that he should live by the pattern of the holy Gospel. He had it written down in a few simple words, and the pope confirmed it. Those who came gave what they had to the poor, and were content with one tunic, patched inside and out, a cord, and breeches. They worked with their hands. And God revealed a greeting for them: the Lord give you peace. Listen to how the Testament keeps saying the Lord gave me. The Lord gave me to begin. The Lord gave me faith in churches. The Lord gave me brothers. He never talks about them as people he recruited. Here's the detail to tell a friend: in his own telling, the people he didn't pick, first the lepers, then the brothers, are exactly where God's direction arrives.
screen: `BITTER, TURNED TO SWEETNESS.` · `THE PATTERN OF THE GOSPEL.` · `ONE TUNIC, A CORD, AND PEACE.` · `THE LORD GAVE ME.` · then, large: `THE LORD GAVE ME BROTHERS.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and bring to mind the people you were given rather than chose: family, classmates, coworkers, neighbors. Pick one who is hard for you, and hold their face for the sit without fixing anything. If you pray, you can offer them the Testament's greeting: the Lord give you peace.
Francis' Testament. Francis of Assisi's short look back at his life, from the lepers to the brothers he was given.
Hold onto this: the Lord gave me brothers, and no manual came with them. See you tomorrow.

Francis of Assisi.meaning: an Italian friar who wrote the Canticle and the Testament

Testament.meaning: Francis's short text looking back on his life

lepers.meaning: people with leprosy, kept apart from others

pope.meaning: the bishop of Rome, head of the Catholic Church
